reading.body:
Glean is an enterprise search and AI agent platform built around permission-aware retrieval and data governance, designed to let organizations find information and automate workflows across 100+ connected data sources while maintaining access controls.

The company's positioning around security and explainability as core design principles rather than bolt-on features reflects a constraint real enterprises face: AI tools that cannot respect existing permissions and audit trails create compliance and operational risk. This matters for AI in the enterprise because most organizations cannot simply move their data into a general-purpose model. Glean's architecture assumes data stays distributed across legacy systems and requires the AI to respect the same access rules humans do.

The data shows Glean operates in California and counts large organizations like Booking.com, Ericsson, and Zillow as customers, with at least one reporting high internal adoption. This does not reveal revenue, growth rate, compute requirements, or how much infrastructure Glean's own platform consumes. It also does not show how many of the 100+ connectors are actively used, or whether the platform's power consumption scales linearly or nonlinearly with the number of organizations it serves. The registered MCP server suggests some standardization of how external applications can query or extend Glean's capabilities, but the available facts do not explain what that integration looks like at scale.

profile_text.body:
Glean is a for-profit startup founded in 2019 and headquartered in Palo Alto, CA, that describes itself as an enterprise AI platform connected to a company's internal data. The platform is positioned around three broad capabilities: finding information, creating content, and automating work through AI agents. The company emphasizes that its approach is built for enterprise use from the start, with security, explainability, and permission-aware retrieval as stated design principles.

The core product, also called Glean, is categorized as an enterprise AI platform with more than 100 connectors to external data sources and data access governance features. It supports enterprise search, an AI assistant, and agent-building in natural language. The site references deployments at Booking.com, Ericsson, GCash, and Zillow, with Zillow noting an 80% adoption rate. Glean also appears in the MCP registry under the identifier co.gleanit/gleanit, covering search, reading, and writing of highlights, notes, screenshots, collections, projects, and tags within the Gleanit application.

The held facts indicate Glean has a notable legal exposure footprint in California, with 181 cases on record in that state, though no specific litigation details are provided in the available data. No SEC filings or patent records are noted in the current held facts.
